facts.fact: Oracle Fusion Cloud EPM subscriptions are bought by contacting Oracle Sales (web chat or 'Contact sales'), and after the order Oracle emails the designated initial contact with activation and provisioning instructions (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/idcs_buy_epm_cloud.html).

The Oracle Fusion Cloud EPM docs offer a 'Request a Demo' path but describe no self-service trial (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/idcs_buy_epm_cloud.html).

The Cloud EPM hierarchy is cloud account (tenancy) > subscription > environments; the Cloud Account Name is the tenancy, cannot be changed, appears in login URLs, and several subscriptions can be activated into one cloud account (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/idcs_opc_key_concepts.html).
Cloud EPM environments are created in the Oracle Cloud Console (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/idcs_opc_key_concepts.html).

facts.target: OCI IAM Identity Domain Administrator role
facts.fact: An identity domain is where Identity Domain Administrators manage Cloud EPM users, and several subscriptions can share one identity domain (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/idcs_opc_key_concepts.html).

A Cloud EPM subscription includes exactly one test and one production environment, designated at creation; more stages (for example dev, test, acceptance, production) require buying another subscription for the extra two environments (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/creating_an_epm_cloud_environment.html).

Creating a Cloud EPM environment needs the OCI Account Administrator role (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/creating_an_epm_cloud_environment.html).

A Cloud EPM environment name becomes part of the URL and cannot be changed; defaults place it in the home region, default compartment and default identity domain, and test and production can sit in different regions, compartments and identity domains (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/creating_an_epm_cloud_environment.html).

Cloud EPM administrator onboarding starts when the Cloud Account Owner (Tenancy Administrator) delegates the administrator role, and the delegate gets an email from oraclecloudadmin_ww@oracle.com titled 'Action Required: Please Activate Your Services' (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmck/epm_cloud_checklist_id_domain_admin.html).

On OCI (Gen 2) the Cloud EPM production URL is https://<instance>-<cloudaccount>.epm.<region>.ocs.oraclecloud.com/epmcloud (for example https://acme-epmidm.epm.us-phoenix-1.ocs.oraclecloud.com/epmcloud) and test adds -test after the instance name (https://acme-test-epmidm.epm.us-phoenix-1.ocs.oraclecloud.com/epmcloud) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsus/1_user_epm_cloud_accessing_sample_urls_gen2.html).

The Cloud Account Name segment of the Cloud EPM OCI (Gen 2) URL was formerly called the Identity Domain Name (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsus/1_user_epm_cloud_accessing_sample_urls_gen2.html).

New Cloud EPM and EDM subscriptions run on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure using OCI IAM ('OCI (Gen 2)' or 'Cloud EPM Gen 2') (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsus/1_user_epm_cloud_accessing_sample_urls.html).

New EDM subscriptions run on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure using OCI IAM (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsus/1_user_epm_cloud_accessing_sample_urls.html).

Oracle Cloud Classic is legacy for Cloud EPM as of 2026-11-14; some customers remain on it and use the separate Classic URL format (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/1_epm_cloud_accessing_sample_urls_classic.html).

On a client engagement an engineer should ask for the test and production environment URLs, an identity domain user with the right application role (normally Service Administrator for automation), an OAuth 2 client ID registered by the Identity Domain Administrator (public client with Device Code and Refresh Token grants) plus the environment's scope, any Network Perimeter IP ranges that must include the runner's egress IP, and the environment's daily maintenance start time (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

A Cloud EPM automation user normally needs the Service Administrator application role (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmck/epm_cloud_checklist_id_domain_admin.html).

facts.target: OCI IAM Identity Domain Administrator role
facts.fact: The Cloud EPM OAuth 2 client ID is registered by the Identity Domain Administrator as a public client with Device Code and Refresh Token grants (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

Any Cloud EPM Network Perimeter IP ranges must include the automation runner's egress IP (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmck/epm_cloud_checklist_id_domain_admin.html).

An engineer starting a Cloud EPM engagement should ask for the environment's daily maintenance start time (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmck/epm_cloud_checklist_id_domain_admin.html).

Cloud EPM identity is OCI IAM identity domains, the successor to Oracle Identity Cloud Service (IDCS); Oracle EPM docs still often say 'Oracle Identity Cloud' or 'IDCS' for this layer (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/idcs_opc_key_concepts.html).

Users, groups, sign-on policies, MFA, SSO federation and OAuth clients for Cloud EPM are managed in the identity domain tied to the environment (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/administrator_roles_defined_at_the_domain_level.html).

facts.fact: Oracle supports Basic Authentication for Cloud EPM REST APIs, but recommends OAuth 2 as more secure (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/published_apis_through_external_ai_tools.html).

Oracle supports OAuth 2 for Cloud EPM REST APIs and recommends it over Basic Authentication as more secure (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/published_apis_through_external_ai_tools.html).

EPM Automate supports both Basic Authentication and OAuth 2, and Oracle recommends OAuth 2 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_automate_oauth.html).

Cloud EPM REST Basic Auth uses the Authorization: Basic header with a username of identitydomain.username or just username; the identity domain name appears in the Activity Report and in the URL between epm- (or epm-test-) and the next dot (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/authentication_overview.html).

Oracle's Classic-vs-OCI comparison says Classic used identitydomain.username for Basic Auth while OCI uses the plain username; the page could not be fetched, so this comes from a search snippet and the Narrative Reporting REST guide (unverified) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/idcs_oci_classic_diffs.html).

EPM Automate and EPM Agent use basic authentication, which does not accept SSO credentials, so these users must keep identity domain (traditional) credentials (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/3_sso_config_chap_enable_idm_credentials.html).

The EPM Agent uses basic authentication, which does not accept SSO credentials, so its user must keep identity domain credentials (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/3_sso_config_chap_enable_idm_credentials.html).
Cloud EPM basic authentication does not accept SSO credentials (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/3_sso_config_chap_enable_idm_credentials.html).
epmautomate login is not supported for basic-auth users with MFA (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_login.html).

Cloud EPM REST APIs cannot be run by users configured for Basic Authentication with MFA (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/published_apis_through_external_ai_tools.html).
OAuth 2 for Cloud EPM REST is a user-context public client, not client credentials (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

facts.target: OCI IAM Identity Domain Administrator role
facts.fact: The Identity Domain Administrator registers a 'Mobile Application' (public client) integrated app, adds the EPM resources, sets each EPM base URL (without /epmcloud) as a secondary audience, enables 'Allow token refresh', and selects only the Refresh Token and Device Code grants (not Implicit) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

For Cloud EPM REST, other OAuth grants (Authorization Code, Resource Owner Password, Assertion) are allowed only if the token is in an end-user context (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

The Cloud EPM OAuth scope is urn:opc:serviceInstanceID=<SERVICE_INSTANCE_ID>urn:opc:resource:consumer::all, with ' offline_access' appended when requesting the first refresh token (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

Scopes for more than one EPM environment cannot be requested in one OAuth request, and a token works only for the environment it was issued for (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

Bootstrap Cloud EPM OAuth with POST https://idcs-<id>.identity.oraclecloud.com/oauth2/v1/device and response_type=device_code; a human signs in at verification_uri as the user who will invoke the APIs and enters the user_code; POST .../oauth2/v1/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code returns the first refresh token, later calls use grant_type=refresh_token, and the API is called with Authorization: Bearer <access token> (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).
In the Cloud EPM device-code flow the user_code expires in 300 seconds (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

The Cloud EPM OAuth 2 public client uses the device-code flow to get the first refresh token, then rotates refresh tokens (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

Cloud EPM OAuth access tokens last 1 hour (sample responses show expires_in: 3600); refresh tokens expire after 7 days and are single use, each refresh returns a new one that must replace the old one, and Oracle advises refreshing at least every 6 days for unattended jobs (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).
Service Administrators can change Cloud EPM OAuth token expiry on the service's OAuth configuration page (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

Scripts that share a Cloud EPM refresh token fail at random with invalid_grant 'The token has already been consumed'; run the device-code bootstrap once per script, and all scripts can share one client_id (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

With OAuth, the Cloud EPM access log shows the user name (as with basic auth) but not the client ID or token, so an automation account's actions are attributed to the user who completed the device-code sign-in (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

facts.fact: For EPM Automate OAuth, run epmautomate encrypt REFRESH_TOKEN ENCRYPTION_KEY PASSWORD_FILE.epw ClientID=CLIENT_ID, then epmautomate login <ignoredUsername> OAuth2.epw <URL> (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_automate_oauth.html).

With OAuth, the EPM Automate login USERNAME argument is ignored and taken from the token; OAuth is enforced per application, and basic auth still works when OAuth is enabled (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_login.html).

The 25.10 readiness note 'Login EPM Automate Command Documentation Clarification When Using oAuth2 Token' (October 2025) documents that the username is ignored when an OAuth 2 token file is used (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2025/epm-oct25/25oct-epm-wn-f41517.htm).

The EPM Automate commands addUsers, removeUsers, assignRole and unassignRole require basic authentication; all other EPM Automate commands work with OAuth 2.0 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_login.html).

Cloud EPM REST user and role APIs include Add Users to an Identity Domain (v2, POST /interop/rest/security/v2/users/add) and Assign Role (v1, PUT /interop/rest/security/v1/users with jobtype=ASSIGN_ROLE) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/lcm_add_user_to_identity_domain_v2.html).

The Cloud EPM REST Add Users and Assign Role pages include both -u user:password and Authorization: Bearer cURL samples, unlike the EPM Automate equivalents that require basic auth (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/lcm_assign_role.html).

epmautomate encrypt PASSWORD|REFRESH_TOKEN KEY PASSWORD_FILE [ClientID=...] [ProxyServerPassword=...] creates an .epw password file; any application role can run it (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_encrypt.html).

EPM Automate password files use the .epw extension and are encrypted with AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding(256); corporate (SSO) credentials cannot be encrypted or used (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_encrypt.html).

The default location of EPM Automate .epw files is ProgramData\Oracle\EPM Automate on Windows and the current directory on Linux (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_encrypt.html).

epmautomate login USERNAME PASSWORD|PASSWORD_FILE URL [IDENTITYDOMAIN] [ProxyServerUserName=...] [ProxyServerPassword=...] [ProxyServerDomain=...] [KeystorePassword=...] signs in; IDENTITYDOMAIN is derived from the URL and ignored (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_login.html).

EPM Automate login supports vanity and API gateway URLs (for example Apigee), and proxy authentication supports Basic, Digest, Kerberos, Negotiate and NTLM but not SOCKS (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_login.html).

To connect Fusion AI Agent Studio to Cloud EPM or EDM REST, an Identity Domain Administrator of the EPM domain creates a confidential application, enables Client Credentials and JWT assertion, changes the client type to Trusted, imports a public certificate (the private key stays in AI Agent Studio), and sets the Token Issuance Policy to Specific with EPM service resources and scopes (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/create_a_confidential_application_for_epm_integration_with_fusion_ai_agent_studio.html).

Oracle Fusion AI Agent Studio integrates with Cloud EPM and EDM REST APIs through a Trusted confidential application in the EPM identity domain (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/create_a_confidential_application_for_epm_integration_with_fusion_ai_agent_studio.html).

Oracle Fusion AI Agent Studio can connect to EDM REST APIs using the same Trusted confidential application pattern as Cloud EPM (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/create_a_confidential_application_for_epm_integration_with_fusion_ai_agent_studio.html).

facts.target: OCI IAM Identity Domain Administrator role
facts.fact: The Trusted confidential application for AI Agent Studio is created by an Identity Domain Administrator of the EPM domain, and it is the only documented confidential-client pattern for EPM (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/create_a_confidential_application_for_epm_integration_with_fusion_ai_agent_studio.html).
Cloud EPM human SSO is SAML 2.0 federation in the identity domain (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmck/epm_cloud_checklist_id_domain_admin.html).

Supported SAML 2.0 identity providers for Cloud EPM SSO include Microsoft Entra ID, Oracle Identity Federation, Okta, Ping Identity PingFederate and Shibboleth (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/3_sso_config_chap_idcs_oci_azure.html).
Okta is a supported SAML 2.0 identity provider for Cloud EPM SSO (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmck/epm_cloud_checklist_id_domain_admin.html).

Ping Identity PingFederate is a supported SAML 2.0 identity provider for Cloud EPM SSO (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmck/epm_cloud_checklist_id_domain_admin.html).

For Cloud EPM SSO in Entra, use the 'Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Console' gallery app with Identifier https://idcs-<id>.identity.oraclecloud.com:443/fed, Reply URL https://idcs-<id>.identity.oraclecloud.com:443/fed/v1/sp/sso, Logout .../fed/v1/sp/slo, and a Name ID (for example user.mail) matching the domain's requested NameID format (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/3_sso_config_chap_idcs_oci_azure_config.html).

SSO-enabled Cloud EPM environments show 'Company Sign-In' and 'Traditional Cloud Account Sign-In' by default; an Identity Domain Administrator can hide traditional sign-in for browser users by removing 'Username-Password' from the default IdP policy rule, but integration accounts still need identity domain credentials (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/3_sso_config_chap_enable_idm_credentials.html).

facts.fact: SCIM can optionally be used to sync users and groups into the Cloud EPM identity domain from systems such as Microsoft Entra ID (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmck/epm_cloud_checklist_id_domain_admin.html).

Users and groups can be synced via SCIM into the Cloud EPM identity domain from Microsoft Entra ID (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmck/epm_cloud_checklist_id_domain_admin.html).

Bulk user creation in the identity domain works via epmautomate addUsers or the REST API Add Users to an Identity Domain (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/iam_chapter_intro.html).

facts.target: OCI IAM Identity Domain Administrator role
facts.fact: The Identity Domain Administrator and Security Administrator configure MFA and authentication factors for Cloud EPM in OCI IAM (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/administrator_roles_defined_at_the_domain_level.html).

The Security Administrator can configure MFA and authentication factors for Cloud EPM in OCI IAM (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/administrator_roles_defined_at_the_domain_level.html).

Cloud EPM users enroll an authenticator app (Oracle Mobile Authenticator, Google Authenticator) via 'Enable Secure Verification' (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/appman_access_rerequisites.html).

Cloud EPM documents no identity type made for AI agents and no keyless or workload identity federation (for example from GitHub Actions or other clouds); automation runs as an identity domain user via Basic Auth or user-context OAuth refresh tokens (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

Oracle's EPM Agent Skills Shared Authentication skill documents only Basic Auth from a private config file (URL, name, username, password) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/shared_authentication.html).

From the May 2026 (26.05) update, Cloud EPM labels Service Administrator, Power User, User and Viewer 'Application Role' (previously 'Predefined Roles') (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-may26/26may-epm-wn-f47257.htm).

From the May 2026 (26.05) update, business-process-specific Cloud EPM roles (previously 'application roles') are called 'granular roles' (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-may26/26may-epm-wn-f47257.htm).
In June 2026 (26.06) the Access Control tab 'Manage Application Roles' became 'Manage Granular Roles' (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-jun26/26jun-epm-wn-f49898.htm).

Older Cloud EPM docs and scripts use the old role names ('Predefined Roles' for the four domain-level roles and 'application roles' for business-process roles) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-apr26/26apr-epm-wn-f40977.htm).

The four Cloud EPM application roles form a hierarchy, Service Administrator > Power User > User > Viewer, in which each higher role inherits the lower roles' access and what each role grants varies by business process (https://docs.oracle.com/cloud/latest/epm-common/CGSAD/4_managing_epm_cloud_users_roles_predefined_roles.htm).
The Cloud EPM Service Administrator role sits above Power User and inherits its access (https://docs.oracle.com/cloud/latest/epm-common/CGSAD/4_managing_epm_cloud_users_roles_predefined_roles.htm).
The Cloud EPM Power User role sits above User and inherits its access (https://docs.oracle.com/cloud/latest/epm-common/CGSAD/4_managing_epm_cloud_users_roles_predefined_roles.htm).
The Cloud EPM User role sits above Viewer and inherits its access (https://docs.oracle.com/cloud/latest/epm-common/CGSAD/4_managing_epm_cloud_users_roles_predefined_roles.htm).

Non-Service Administrator access in Cloud EPM also depends on each dimension's 'Apply Security' setting, which Oracle recommends enabling (https://docs.oracle.com/cloud/latest/epm-common/CGSAD/4_managing_epm_cloud_users_roles_predefined_roles.htm).

Enterprise Data Management uses only Service Administrator and User; assigning Power User or Viewer in EDM grants no privileges (https://docs.oracle.com/cloud/latest/epm-common/CGSAD/4_managing_epm_cloud_users_roles_predefined_roles.htm).

Users without an application role do not appear in EPM or EDM environments, and EPM Automate login then fails with 'User does not exist for this application' (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/tsepm/7_tips_and_tricks_troubleshoot_access_issues_epm_automate_insufficient_priv.html).

Most EPM Automate commands are restricted to Service Administrators; error 'EPMAT-9: Insufficient Privileges To Perform the Operation' means the user's role does not permit the command (for example a User running downloadFile) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/tsepm/7_tips_and_tricks_troubleshoot_access_issues_epm_automate_insufficient_priv.html).

epmautomate importData JOB_NAME [FILE] errorFile=... and epmautomate importMetadata JOB_NAME [FILE] errorFile=... require the Service Administrator role, and the job must already be defined in the Jobs console (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_import_data.html).

EPM Automate runDataRule requires Service Administrator or Power User, and runBusinessRule requires Service Administrator or Power User (only when Launch access to the rule is granted) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_run_business_rule.html).

facts.target: Cloud EPM Migrations - Administer granular role
facts.fact: EPM Automate exportSnapshot, importSnapshot, copySnapshotFromInstance, cloneEnvironment and setDailyMaintenanceStartTime each require 'Service Administrator' or 'Any application role and the Migrations - Administer granular role' (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_export_snapshot.html).

facts.target: OCI IAM Identity Domain Administrator role
facts.fact: importSnapshot ... importUsers=true needs the Identity Domain Administrator role, otherwise the Migration Status Report shows 'User ... is not authorized' (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_import_snapshot.html).

cloneEnvironment UsersAndApplicationRoles=true needs a target Service Administrator who also holds Identity Domain Administrator, and the Identity Domain Administrator assignment itself is not cloned (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_clone_environment.html).

epmautomate addUsers FILE.csv [userPassword=...] [resetPassword=true|false] requires 'Identity Domain Administrator and any application role'; the users are created in the identity domain and can reach every environment that shares it (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_add_users.html).

epmautomate assignRole FILE.csv ROLE requires Service Administrator, or Identity Domain Administrator plus any application role, for application roles; for granular roles it requires Service Administrator, or any application role plus the 'Access Control - Manage' granular role (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_assign_roles.html).

facts.target: Cloud EPM Access Control - Manage granular role
facts.fact: Assigning granular roles with epmautomate assignRole requires Service Administrator, or any application role plus the 'Access Control - Manage' granular role (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_assign_roles.html).

A Service Administrator can assign Cloud EPM application roles without being a domain admin; customers can ask Oracle to restrict application-role assignment to Identity Domain Administrators (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/administrator_roles_defined_at_the_domain_level.html).

facts.source: OCI IAM Identity Domain Administrator role
facts.fact: The Identity Domain Administrator can run addUsers, removeUsers, updateUsers, assignRole, unassignRole, roleAssignmentAuditReport and invalidLoginReport only if also given a Cloud EPM application role (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/administrator_roles_defined_at_the_domain_level.html).

OCI IAM defines seven domain-level admin roles with EPM command limits: Identity Domain Administrator, Security Administrator, Application Administrator, User Administrator, User Manager, Help Desk Administrator and Audit Administrator (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/administrator_roles_defined_at_the_domain_level.html).

Security Administrator is one of the seven OCI IAM domain-level admin roles relevant to Cloud EPM (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/administrator_roles_defined_at_the_domain_level.html).

facts.source: OCI IAM Help Desk Administrator role
facts.fact: Help Desk Administrator is one of the seven OCI IAM domain-level admin roles relevant to Cloud EPM (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/administrator_roles_defined_at_the_domain_level.html).

The OCI IAM Application Administrator cannot run the EPM commands assignRole or unassignRole (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/administrator_roles_defined_at_the_domain_level.html).

The OCI IAM User Administrator cannot run the EPM commands addUsers, removeUsers or updateUsers (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/administrator_roles_defined_at_the_domain_level.html).

The OCI IAM User Manager cannot run the EPM commands removeUsers or updateUsers (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/administrator_roles_defined_at_the_domain_level.html).

The OCI IAM Audit Administrator cannot run the EPM commands roleAssignmentAuditReport or invalidLoginReport (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/administrator_roles_defined_at_the_domain_level.html).

Least-privilege pattern synthesized from per-command role lists: a pipeline that only runs data rules and business rules can use Power User (with rule Launch access); one that runs importData, importMetadata or most file operations needs Service Administrator; snapshot work can use any application role plus 'Migrations - Administer'; user provisioning additionally needs Identity Domain Administrator and, in EPM Automate, basic auth rather than OAuth (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_run_data_rule.html).

On the client side the Account Administrator creates Cloud EPM environments (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/creating_an_epm_cloud_environment.html).

facts.target: OCI IAM Identity Domain Administrator role
facts.fact: The Identity Domain Administrator creates Cloud EPM users, OAuth clients, SSO federation, sign-on policies and the Network Perimeter (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmck/epm_cloud_checklist_id_domain_admin.html).

facts.target: OCI IAM Identity Domain Administrator role
facts.fact: The Network Perimeter for Cloud EPM is set up by the Identity Domain Administrator (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmck/epm_cloud_checklist_id_domain_admin.html).

The Service Administrator assigns application and granular roles and manages Access Control groups in the Cloud EPM environment (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmck/epm_cloud_checklist_id_domain_admin.html).

facts.fact: A future Cloud EPM update (date not given in the 26.04 notes) will require Power Users to have write access, not just read access, to a folder before creating forms, dashboards or subfolders in it (EPCM, FCCS, FreeForm, Planning, Tax Reporting) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-apr26/26apr-epm-wn-t74023.htm).
By default only Service Administrators can download EPM compliance reports (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/accessing_soc_compliance_reps.html).

Non-Service Administrators need an OCI IAM policy such as 'Allow group G to {EPM_COMPLIANCEDOC_INSPECT, EPM_COMPLIANCEDOC_READ} in tenancy' to download EPM compliance reports (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/accessing_soc_compliance_reps.html).

EPM compliance document access for non-admins uses the OCI IAM policy permission EPM_COMPLIANCEDOC_INSPECT, together with EPM_COMPLIANCEDOC_READ, granted in tenancy (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/accessing_soc_compliance_reps.html).

In May 2026 (26.05) Oracle removed setIPAllowList, getIPAllowList and the IPAllowList REST APIs (deprecated earlier) and replaced them with the identity-domain Network Perimeter (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-may26/26may-epm-wn-f46472.htm).

The per-environment Cloud EPM IP allowlist commands and REST APIs were removed in May 2026 (26.05); older EPM Automate versions that run these commands are ignored (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-apr26/26apr-epm-wn-f46471.htm).

The Network Perimeter applies allowed or blocked IPs and CIDRs identity-domain-wide and also protects Cloud Console (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_set_ip_allowlist.html).

To migrate from per-environment allowlists, export each environment's list with getIPAllowlist (before removal), merge the unique IPs and CIDRs, and add them to the identity domain's Network Perimeter in Oracle Cloud Console; while both existed, a source IP had to be in both lists (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/migrating_from_ip_allowlist_per_environment_to_network_perimeter_for_an_identity_domain.html).

The Network Perimeter restricts sign-in to listed IPs and ranges for all EPM and EDM environments in the designated identity domain (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/setting_up_network_perimeter_for_oci_gen_2_epm_cloud.html).

With a Network Perimeter, inbound calls from other EPM environments (copySnapshotFromInstance, cloneEnvironment, Copy Application Snapshot REST, Navigation Flows) are blocked unless the source region's outbound IP is added (for example us-ashburn-1 = 130.35.200.71); within one region, add 240.0.0.0/4 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/tsepm/outbound_ip_address_cloud_dc.html).

facts.target: OCI IAM Identity Domain Administrator role
facts.fact: The default sign-on policy lets any user with an application role sign in to Cloud EPM with a username and password; an Identity Domain Administrator can add a custom policy (for example, only Service Administrators) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/sec_compliance_sign-on_policy.html).

Oracle does not support customer VPN connections to Cloud EPM; private connectivity uses an OCI Service Gateway (needs an OCI IaaS subscription in the same region) or an OCI VCN over FastConnect plus Service Gateway (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/configuration_vpn.html).

Private connectivity to Cloud EPM uses an OCI Service Gateway, which needs an OCI IaaS subscription in the same region (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/configuration_vpn.html).
Cloud EPM can be reached privately from an OCI VCN over FastConnect plus Service Gateway (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/configuration_vpn.html).

From the 26.04 notes, Manage Connections blocks creating or modifying connections whose URL uses an IP address; use hostnames (EPCM, FCCS, FreeForm, Planning, Tax Reporting) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-apr26/26apr-epm-wn-t74023.htm).

Each Cloud EPM environment reserves one hour a day for patching, the Environment Backup and the 'Artifact Snapshot', and the Activity Report; the default start is between 10:00 p.m. and 1:00 a.m. in the hosting region's local time, and users are logged off with a 15-minute warning (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/6_house_keeping_tasks_daily_maintenance_tasks.html).

During daily maintenance, for Planning, FCCS, Tax Reporting and EPCM, operations such as data and metadata import, Refresh Database and Data Integration run via EPM Automate, REST or the Job Console schedule are blocked (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/6_house_keeping_tasks_daily_maintenance_tasks.html).

For EDM all operations are blocked during the daily maintenance window (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/6_house_keeping_tasks_daily_maintenance_tasks.html).

facts.fact: epmautomate setDailyMaintenanceStartTime "HH:MM [TZ]" sets the daily maintenance start (UTC if no zone); it will not change if maintenance has not run in the last 36 hours (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_set_daily_maint_start.html).

The Cloud EPM daily maintenance start time can be set with PUT /interop/rest/v2/maintenance/setdailymaintenancestarttime (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/lcm_update_maintenance_time_v2.html).

Since April 2024 Oracle randomizes the Cloud EPM daily maintenance start minute when the customer has not set one (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2024/epm-apr24/24apr-epm-wn-f32927.htm).

cloneEnvironment terminates if the source's daily maintenance starts during cloning, so automation should be scheduled clear of both environments' windows (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_clone_environment.html).

New commercial Cloud EPM orders are provisioned to OCI data centers and activated in the region named in the customer's Ordering Document; region names come from search snippets because the location page returned 404 (unverified) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/tsepm/choosing_epm_cloud_data_centers_and_regions.html).

Cloud EPM regions span the commercial OC1 realm (APAC, Europe, Middle East, North America, South Africa, South America and Morocco), US Government (OC2), US Defense (OC3), UK Government (OC4), Oracle EU Sovereign Cloud (OC19, eu-frankfurt-2, eu-madrid-2) and Dedicated Region Cloud@Customer realms (OC9, OC21, OC29, OC36, OC42, OC52) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/tsepm/opc_gen_2_regions.html).

Per a search snippet of the migration page (404), Oracle states all Classic commercial data center EPM environments were migrated to OCI, with UK Government Classic still planned (unverified) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/tsepm/opc_oci_mig_assist.html).

Oracle-managed migration of Classic US Government EPM environments to OCI was announced in December 2024 and April 2025 readiness notes (unverified) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2025/epm-apr25/25apr-epm-wn-f38019.htm).

Oracle lists Cloud EPM security features including TLS 1.2/1.3, Transparent Data Encryption and OCI Block Volume encryption, FIPS 140-2 HSM keys, Bring Your Own Key, data masking, Restrict Data Access by Oracle, WAF, API gateway support, virus scan on uploads, Tor blocking, maximum session duration and idle timeout, an immutable and air-gapped backup in a secondary region, access logs and SIEM integration (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/3_info_security_epm_cloud.html).

facts.source: Cloud EPM Restrict Data Access by Oracle
facts.fact: setRestrictedDataAccess (EPM Automate) or the Set Restricted Data Access REST API stops Service Administrators from submitting application snapshots to Oracle; snapshot submission is already unavailable in OC2 and OC4 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/restrict_data_access_by_oracle.html).

Cloud EPM audit reports include the Activity Report, access log, User Login Report, Role Assignment Audit, userAuditReport, groupAssignmentAuditReport and invalidLoginReport, plus audit logs in Oracle Cloud Console (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmck/epm_cloud_checklist_id_domain_admin.html).
The Cloud EPM OAuth access log shows the user but not the client ID (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

Cloud EPM compliance attestations SOC 1 (SSAE 18), SOC 2, Bridge Letter, ISO Certificate, Disaster Recovery Evidence Document and Security Assessment Report are downloaded from Identity & Security > Compliance in Cloud Console (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/accessing_soc_compliance_reps.html).
Cloud EPM AI and GenAI features are EPM Enterprise only (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/1_about_epm_cloud_new_sku_changes.html).
Cloud EPM environments not on 26.04 or later by the end of July 2026 (26.07) lose GenAI access (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-apr26/26apr-epm-wn-t74023.htm).
In-product EPM LLMs reference OCI Generative AI (GPT-OSS) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/llm_availability_and_usage_in_epm.html).

The GPT-OSS model referenced by in-product EPM LLMs is offered through OCI Generative AI (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/llm_availability_and_usage_in_epm.html).

Oracle's EPM AI pages fetched on 2026-11-14 make no statement on whether customer data trains models or how to opt out (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/llm_availability_and_usage_in_epm.html).

facts.fact: For external AI tools calling Cloud EPM REST APIs, Oracle says the customer owns model selection, prompt design, security boundaries, auditability and output review; EPM still applies data and business-process security to each request (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/published_apis_through_external_ai_tools.html).

EPM Standard is one of two current Cloud EPM subscription tiers, aimed at small and mid-sized businesses (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/1_about_epm_cloud_new_sku_changes.html).

EPM Standard includes Planning modules only, one ASO and one BSO cube, and no custom Groovy, Custom Planning, FreeForm, Sales Planning, Strategic Workforce Planning or Predictive Cash Forecasting (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/1_about_epm_cloud_new_sku_changes.html).

EPM Enterprise is the full-suite Cloud EPM tier: multiple cubes, Groovy, Enterprise Journals, Transaction Matching, Tax Provisions, CbCR, Pillar Two, EPCM and PCM, Narrative Reporting Report Notes, all AI and GenAI features, and IPM (except AutoPredict, which Standard Planning also gets) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/1_about_epm_cloud_new_sku_changes.html).

Only users with application roles (Service Administrator, Power User, User, Viewer) count toward the Cloud EPM Named Users license; users assigned only a domain-level administrator role do not count (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/administrator_roles_defined_at_the_domain_level.html).

Every Cloud EPM automation or integration account with an application role consumes a named-user seat (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/administrator_roles_defined_at_the_domain_level.html).

Oracle provides a sample script that counts licensed Cloud EPM users from epmautomate roleAssignmentReport output (one count per user login) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/sample_script_5_license.html).

Third-party licensing advisers report that EPM Enterprise is sold per Hosted Named User per month or per Hosted Employee (headcount) per month (secondary) (https://redresscompliance.com/oracle-epm-cloud-licensing-modules-pricing.html).

Hosted Employee is a per-headcount-per-month Cloud EPM licensing metric; the Oracle subscriptions page also references hosted-employee and hosted-record limits for EDM (secondary) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/1_about_epm_cloud_new_sku_changes.html).

Advisers cite about USD 250 per named user per month for EPM Standard (10-user minimum), viewed 2026-11-14; Oracle's own price list returned HTTP 403 (secondary) (unverified) (https://redresscompliance.com/oracle-epm-cloud-licensing-modules-pricing.html).

Advisers cite about USD 500 per named user per month for EPM Enterprise (25-user minimum) and about USD 40 per hosted employee per month for large organisations, viewed 2026-11-14 (secondary) (unverified) (https://redresscompliance.com/oracle-epm-cloud-licensing-modules-pricing.html).

Under Hosted Named User, every Cloud EPM service or integration user with an application role is a billable named user; under Hosted Employee, seats are headcount-based (secondary) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/administrator_roles_defined_at_the_domain_level.html).

Oracle documents no separate per-token EPM charge for agent use through EPM Agent Skills or REST, but AI features require EPM Enterprise (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/using_ai_agents_for_cloud_epm.html).

facts.target: AI Agent Studio for Fusion Cloud Applications entitlement
facts.fact: EPM Assistants require a separate AI Agent Studio for Fusion Cloud Applications entitlement (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/using_ai_agents_for_cloud_epm.html).

Unconfirmed: Oracle's official EPM price list (oracle.com/performance-management/pricing and /cloud/price-list) returned HTTP 403, so all prices and metric minimums come only from third-party advisers (https://www.oracle.com/performance-management/pricing/).

Unconfirmed: the Classic-vs-OCI differences page, the data-center location page and the Classic-to-OCI migration page returned 404, so their claims are marked unverified (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/idcs_oci_classic_diffs.html).

Unconfirmed: whether the identity-domain Network Perimeter (with sign-on policy) applies to REST API and EPM Automate calls as well as browser sign-in; Oracle docs only say it limits 'sign-ins' (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/setting_up_network_perimeter_for_oci_gen_2_epm_cloud.html).

Unconfirmed: no Oracle page fetched states whether EPM GenAI features or AI Agent Studio use customer data for model training, or how to opt out (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/llm_availability_and_usage_in_epm.html).

Unconfirmed: no official statement was found on whether a client-credentials (non-user) OAuth token can call general Cloud EPM REST APIs outside the AI Agent Studio Trusted-app pattern; the REST guide says tokens must be in an end-user context (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).
